title: ZSI 375 Versus AMS 800 for Male Stress Urinary Incontinence: Functional Outcomes and Device Survival at One and Five Years in a Matched Cohort
content: Background/Objectives: We compared functional outcomes and device survival at one and five years in men who received a ZSI 375 or AMS 800 artificial urinary sphincter (AUS) for stress urinary incontinence. Methods: We matched 36 ZSI 375 recipients to 36 AMS 800 recipients in a retrospective cohort of men undergoing implantation for stress urinary incontinence. Preoperative incontinence was severe in 70 men and moderate in two. The primary surgical outcome was time to first revision, including surgery on a single component. Device survival ended at complete removal or replacement. Social continence required use of 0–1 pad per day with the implanted sphincter in place and functioning. Results: During follow-up, 12/36 AMS 800 recipients and 14/36 ZSI 375 recipients underwent revision (hazard ratio for ZSI 375 vs. AMS 800, 0.64, 95% confidence interval 0.25–1.64). Estimated device survival was 86.0% versus 91.7% at one year and 71.0% versus 79.9% at five years (AMS 800 vs. ZSI 375). Social continence with a functioning device was achieved by 23/29 versus 13/29 men at one year (p = 0.013) and 12/16 versus 5/16 at five years (p = 0.039). When any surgical revision counted as failure, the one-year comparison was 21/29 versus 13/29 (p = 0.077). Conclusions: More men with an AMS 800 achieved social continence with a functioning sphincter at both assessments. The study could not establish which device was less likely to require revision. Nonrandom device selection and differences in implantation year limit attribution to device choice.
